title: Fault-line cake
subtitle: geometric band of exposed decoration across a smoothly iced cake
excerpt: A fault-line cake has a horizontal band of exposed decoration, such as sprinkles, flowers, or fruit, running around the middle of the cake, framed by smooth buttercream above and below. The effect is achieved by building up buttercream in two separate coats with the decorative band left bare between them. The levelling of each buttercream coat is the part that requires patience.
sourceNotes: Contemporary cake decorating technique, widely documented in online cake decorating communities and competition baking (public domain knowledge base).

glossaryTerms.definition: A thin first layer of buttercream applied to a cake to seal in crumbs before the final smooth coat is added.
A soft icing made from butter and icing sugar, used to coat and fill layered cakes.
The horizontal strip of exposed decoration running around the middle of a fault-line cake, framed by smooth buttercream above and below.

content.text: A fault-line cake has a band of decoration running around its middle, with smooth
buttercream
above and below it. The technique uses two separate buttercream coats, applied one at a time. The decoration goes in between the two coats, filled and chilled before the second coat is added. The
fault-line band
needs sharp edges. You need a ruler, an icing smoother, and a cold firm cake at each stage.

A layered and filled cake on a board. Firm buttercream (Swiss meringue or American style). Offset palette knife and icing spatula. Icing smoother. Cake turntable. Ruler. Decorative elements for the band: sprinkles, edible flowers, freeze-dried fruit, or similar.
Method
Crumb coat and chill
Apply a thin
crumb coat
of buttercream over the whole cake: sides and top. Scrape it back to a very thin, even layer using the icing smoother.
Chill the crumb-coated cake for at least 30 minutes, until completely firm. The crumb coat must be set solid before the next stage.
Use a ruler and the back of a palette knife to lightly mark the height of the fault-line band on the chilled cake. A band of 3 to 5 cm works well for most standard layer cakes.
First buttercream coat (lower section)
Apply a thicker coat of buttercream to the lower section of the cake only, up to the bottom edge of the marked fault-line band. Keep the top edge of this coat clean and level.
Smooth the lower section with the icing smoother, holding it vertical against the side and rotating the turntable. Use a ruler to check the height of the upper edge is consistent all the way around.
Applying the decorative band

While the lower buttercream is still soft, press your decorative elements firmly into the exposed band. Work around the cake in sections, pressing each piece gently so it embeds slightly and will not slide.
Fill the band densely and evenly. Gaps will show as dark patches against the cake when the top coat is applied.
Chill the cake for 15 to 20 minutes so the decorations are set in place before applying the upper section of buttercream.
Second buttercream coat (upper section)

Apply buttercream to the upper section and the top of the cake. Bring the edge of the upper coat down to just overlap the top edge of the decorative band, bridging over it slightly to frame it cleanly.
Smooth the upper section with the icing smoother in the same way as the lower section. Keep the smoother clear of the band itself.
Final chill and clean-up
Chill the finished cake for at least 30 minutes. The buttercream must be set firm before trimming the edges of the band.
Use a clean palette knife held horizontal at each edge of the band to trim any buttercream that has crept into the band. Pull the knife towards you in a single stroke.
Return to the refrigerator until ready to serve or display.

attrs.problem: Band is not level around the cake
attrs.avoid: Avoid eyeballing the height; mark it with a ruler before applying the first coat.
attrs.fix: Use a ruler and toothpick to re-mark the band height on the chilled crumb coat before adding the final buttercream layers.

attrs.problem: Decorations slide or drop out of the band
attrs.avoid: Avoid pressing decorations into buttercream that has already chilled; they will not grip.
attrs.fix: Apply decorations immediately after spreading the lower buttercream coat, while the surface is still soft enough to hold them.

attrs.problem: Top edge of the band is not crisp
attrs.avoid: Avoid trimming the band edges while the buttercream is still soft, as it will drag.
attrs.fix: Chill the cake until the buttercream is fully set, then use a palette knife in a single horizontal stroke to trim each edge clean.
